data.name: Artemus
data.long_meaning: In ancient Greek mythology, Artemis was the goddess of the wilderness, the hunt, the wild animals, the mountains, the forests, and the childbirth. Artemus is derived from Artemis, and means 'man's man' or 'butcher' in Greek. It is a name of power and protection.

in_greek.name: Αρτέμος
in_greek.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek goddess Artemis, meaning 'butcher', 'hunter', 'goddess of wilderness', or 'goddess of the hunt'. In the New Testament, it is the name of a disciple of Jesus.

in_english.name: Artemus
in_english.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Artemas, meaning 'Manly, Courageous'.

biblical_reference.note: Artemas was a disciple of Jesus and a companion of St. Luke. He was probably the same person as the one named Drusus in Acts 16:1, and was possibly the bearer of the letter from the church at Ephesus to Paul in Acts 27:1-26.

data.cultural_impact: The name Artemus was popular among early Christians, especially in the Roman Empire. The name could have also been chosen due to the image of Artemis as a powerful and independent goddess, reflecting the strength and resilience of individuals during a time when the Christian faith faced persecution.
